newsitem.title: USA: Norwest says net could top $2 bln in 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Norwest says net could top $2 bln in 5 yrs.

text.p: Norwest Corp said Thursday its annual income of $1.16 billion or $3.07 a share topped the $1.0 billion level for the first time.

"It took Norwest 67 years to earn more than $1 billion in a year, which we achieved in 1996; given our current earnings momentum, it could take us as few as five years to earn the next $1 billion," Dick Kovacevich, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Its 1996 earnings include a $0.03 a share charge for the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF) assessment.
In 1995, Norwest earned $956.0 million or $2.76 a primary share ($2.73 per fully diluted).
In the fourth quarter, Norwest earned $0.81 a share, up from $0.72 a year ago.
Norwest said its provision for credit losses in the fourth quarter rose to $113.6 million, or 1.14 percent of average loans and leases, from $95.9 million or 1.02 percent of loans and leases.
